name: Facet
text: Build the Excava interface in Figma as a clickable prototype first. It lets users test flows without coding, exposing usability flaws early. The trade-off is slower pixel-perfect fidelity, but speed beats perfection for risky flows.

name: Pane
text: The Figma prototype risks users mistaking the polished demo for the real interface—users won’t notice missing states or edge cases because the visual polish masks gaps. A better alternative is to build a low-fidelity wireframe in a tool like Balsamiq first, forcing users to focus on structure over aesthetics; the argument settles when we test both with real users and measure which exposes flaws faster.
